text:
alex: Quick follow-up on the console query authz proposal — wrote up a compact cutover plan (link: https://rwd.infra/rfcs/console-authz-cutover). Wanted to get alignment before we carve up tasks.

cheng: skimmed — big +1 for splitting the policy checks out of the renderer. question: what’s the expected p50 extra latency if we call an external policy engine vs in-process check?

derek: based on earlier benching, external call + single-hop cache is ~1.2–1.8ms median if cache hit, 8–15ms on miss (policy DB lookup). In-process check is ~0.2ms but adds memory and coupling to the renderer.

maria: risk we haven’t quantified: RBAC rule explosion for dashboards with per-entity perms. If we centralize, policy size grows and cold-miss behaviour could kill tail latency. Need TTL strategy.

sofia: proposal: keep policy decision in a lightweight sidecar per renderer pod that keeps a bounded LRU of recent decisions, and offloads policy updates from central engine via push/sync. Sidecar wins network hop locality and avoids rendering process churn.

alex: sidecar idea aligns with earlier runtime goals. tradeoffs: +locality, +work isolation, -extra replica memory and management. central engine: +single source of truth, +easier audits, -network tail risk.

anna: i can run a mini bench today. can you confirm traffic profile to emulate? prefer a 95th percentile target: end-to-end render SLO is 120ms. authz p95 budget should be <15ms.

cheng: we should aim authz p95 < 10ms so renderer has buffer. also track authz p99 separately.

derek: agreeing on metrics. also think about cache warmup window. If sidecar keeps only 5k entries per pod we're golden for most dashboards; for tenant-heavy workloads might need cross-pod cache pre-warming.

maria: can we do a hybrid: sidecar for fast-path decisions + central policy for complex queries (time-bound or attribute-heavy)? fallback to central on miss with circuit-breaker.

sofia: yes — hybrid pattern sounds good. implementation sketch: 1) sidecar maintains LRU + short TTL (30s), 2) sidecar subscribes to policy deltas via stream, 3) on miss, sidecar calls central PDP with backoff and records metrics.

alex: sounds like the cutover phases we should use: 1) dev build with sidecar in staging + synthetic traffic; 2) pilot on internal dashboards only (1% traffic) for 48h with detailed tracing; 3) canary 5% for 24h; 4) gradual ramp with automatic rollback if authz p95 or overall render p95 regresses >5% over baseline.

anna: i’ll run the bench for step 1 and post numbers. quick config snippet for sidecar TTL i’ll test: ```
policy_cache:
  max_entries: 5000
  ttl_seconds: 30
  refresh_window: 10 # proactively refresh hot entries
```

cheng: nice. also add a debug flag to dump cache hit rates per route. we’ll need to instrument: authz_p95, authz_p99, cache_hit_rate, cache_miss_latency, fallback_rate.

derek: ownership: infra-team implements sidecar binary (small go service), eng-platform wires the injector and rollout policy, product+maria validates policy surface. I can take infra tasks if that helps.

maria: product will own policy taxonomy and tests + create a small eval suite (prompted flows) to validate correctness after rollout.

alex: blockers: a) need a PDP API SLA for fallback; b) secure channel for policy stream; c) migration playbook for tenants with huge rule sets.

sofia: for (a) we can host a lightweight replica set in each region with auto-scale; (b) use mTLS + kafka changefeed; (c) for big tenants we can precompute coarse-grained policy entries and fallback to fine-grained central checks only when necessary.

infra-bot: deploy-check: sidecar image built: rwd/console-sidecar:sha256:abcd1234. Staging smoke pipeline queued.

alex: thanks all. next steps: anna post perf numbers, derek start sidecar skeleton, cheng add tracing + metrics dashboard, maria draft migration playbook. I’ll update the RFC with phases and metrics. :thumbsup:

maria: one more ask — include access audit hooks (who evaluated what) in the sidecar logs with sampling off by default. audits are required for enterprise contracts.

derek: ack. will add structured audit event schema (tid, request_id, decision, reason).

anna: bench results: staging synthetic sim (5k req/s, 70/30 cache hit/miss): authz p50=1.3ms, p95=6.9ms, p99=14.6ms; end-to-end render p95=98ms. posting detailed numbers to the eng-platform dashboard.

cheng: those look acceptable. schedule a 1h sync tomorrow to finalize cutover checklist?

alex: scheduled 0900 UTC tomorrow. invite sent. thanks everyone.
